summary: A deep copy must allocate all n cloned nodes and reproduce their next and random fields, imposing an Omega(n) output-size lower bound. The three-pass interleaving method matches it.

optimality.argument: The result must contain n distinct new node objects, each with its value and pointer fields established, so producing the required deep copy takes Omega(n) work. The current method traverses the list three times and performs constant work per node in each pass, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Omitting any source position would omit its required clone or leave one of that clone's fields unconstructed, so all n nodes must contribute to the output.
Interleaving, assigning random pointers, and separating the lists each visit every original node once with constant work.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover null targets, shared targets, repeated values, and self-targeting; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
